pages.text: "Hungry!" Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, grabbed white bread with ashy hands. Grandpa had sprinkled a line of ash along the frozen alley. It was not slippery, so the three had been running there.
Five black finger marks appeared on the bread. "Washing is a bother! Frozen hands hurt even more!" Gugu gobbled, thinking only of running again.
Soon, a tummy went gurgle, gurgle! Gugu stopped running and sat down with a mild stomachache. "Oh, my tummy..."
Steam drifted from the bucket by the door. Grandpa was pouring in stove-warmed water. "The water is warm today, Gugu." Gugu dipped fingertips in.
"Ash carries tiny things you cannot see. Clean hands—yum!" Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, and Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, stood beside Gugu. "Clean hands—yum!"
One—wet both hands. Two—rub with soap until bubbles pile up like snow. Three—rub the backs of your hands and between every finger.
Rinse! Black ash washed away. Gugu dried each finger with a towel. The hands were clean. "Clean hands—yum!"
Gugu picked up fresh bread. No marks this time! "White bread should stay white." Grandpa nodded. The tummy had stopped hurting too. Gugu touched the green bag strap.
At snack time next day, Gugu called first. "Wait! One, wet your hands! Two, bubbly soap! Three, rinse every corner!" The three washed side by side and waved their hands dry.
Grandpa cupped Gugu's hands in his. Clean hands leave no black marks on bread. "No marks now, right? Clean hands—yum!" Gugu smiled.
